cause: The one-type pool rule (_distincts, written by 0.8.2-rc1/J5.T2 in 4a6c3f8) lived in the engine-shared catalog semantic slot, so CommonValidator.validate_spark_spec also refused mixed-type distincts pools SparkGenerator generated on 0.8.1, the None pool included (the in-spec way to get nulls on Spark); the rule is only a NumPy gen_distincts precondition.
context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by dd-code-reviewer in the rc-1 wt-rc review (verdict 2026-11-01T161703Z), probed on tag 0.8.1 and the wt-rc HEAD with Spark 3.5.8 local. Severity HIGH: a contract broken on SparkGenerator's default path for nullable text (Spark refuses null_rate, so a None in the pool is the in-spec way to get nulls). Contract: the operator's version ruling (every grammar change is 0.9.0's) and SPEC 0.8.2 rc-1 §5 (a newly refused spec failed or lost data on 0.8.1). Fixed inside rc-1 by main-thread ruling R16 under the operator's standing order that no rc closes with an open bug.
expected: SparkGenerator accepts and generates the mixed-type pools it generated on 0.8.1; the one-type rule refuses them on DataGenerator, whose NumPy engine fails on them.
repro: cd repos/rand-engine && poetry run python -c "from rand_engine.validators.common_validator import CommonValidator; print(CommonValidator.validate_spark_spec({'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': ['x', 'y', None]}}}))"
solution: _distincts keeps only the non-empty rule; the one-type rule is applied in AdvancedValidator, the NumPy intake, with the same message, so Spark accepts its 0.8.1 pools again and DataGenerator still refuses them (0479659, ruling R16).
symptom: SparkGenerator({'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': ['x', 'y', None]}}}) and a distincts pool [1, 2.5] generate on tag 0.8.1 ('x', 'y', null; 1.0, 2.5) and raise SpecValidationError 'must hold one type' at the wt-rc HEAD, because the shared catalog rule _distincts/_mixed_types (method_specs.py:198-211), a NumPy-engine precondition, also runs on the Spark intake.
title: SparkGenerator refuses a mixed-type distincts pool that generated on 0.8.1

context: Security finding (CWE-526) by dd-code-reviewer in the rc-1 wt-rc review (verdict 2026-11-01T161703Z); block-list item (4) of specs/bugs/AGENTS.md §2, so it lands on the rc-1 wt-rc. Operator ruling 2026-11-01 (AskUserQuestion, verbatim answer): "Scrub child env (Recommended)" — pin the CLI at 2.1.316, which has CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB, install bubblewrap on the runner and set scrub=1. Severity MEDIUM per the reviewer: the CI eval only, non-blocking workflow, operator-owned token.
expected: The eval runs claude -p with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 under bubblewrap on the runner, on a CLI version that implements the scrub, so the agent's subprocesses never see the token.
symptom: evals/run.py:60-62 passes CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to claude -p with --permission-mode dontAsk and Bash, WebFetch and WebSearch allowed; E1 pip-installs whatever package the agent finds, and nothing guarantees the agent's Bash children do not inherit the token, so an installed package could read and exfiltrate it.
title: The CI eval's OAuth token can reach the evaluated agent's shell children
